treasure_bohemian_garnets.name: Bohemian Garnet Cluster
treasure_bohemian_garnets.lore: These blood-red garnets are still held fast in their lump of rock, and the jewellers of Bohemia would set such stones by the hundred in brooch, comb and button. One alone is worth little, though a handful will buy a horse.

treasure_baltic_amber.name: Lump of Baltic Amber
treasure_baltic_amber.lore: Forty million years ago the resin of some tree set hard, and in after ages the sea cast it up on the cold Baltic shore, where Roman traders came a thousand miles along the Amber Road to buy it. Within this lump is a gnat that was imprisoned before ever there were people in the world to set a trap.

treasure_badakhshan_lapis.name: Badakhshan Lapis Stone
treasure_badakhshan_lapis.lore: For six thousand years the folk of Badakhshan have dug this blue stone from their mountains, and when it was ground into ultramarine the painters kept it for their most important robes, since it was dearer than gold. Its golden flecks are pyrite, which for all its name of fool's gold does honest service here.

treasure_burmese_ruby.name: Burmese Ruby
treasure_burmese_ruby.lore: From the Mogok valley in Burma comes this ruby of the red called pigeon's blood. The kings of that land claimed every great stone the miners found, but this one escaped them.

treasure_kashmir_sapphire.name: Kashmir Sapphire
treasure_kashmir_sapphire.lore: In the 1880s the side of a mountain fell away in high Kashmir and laid bare sapphires as softly blue as the cornflower. Within a few years the mine was empty, and no stones like these have been found since that time.

treasure_golconda_diamond.name: Golconda Diamond
treasure_golconda_diamond.lore: This diamond came from the mines by Golconda that gave the world the Koh-i-Noor and the Hope, in that land of India which for two thousand years was the only known home of such stones, and it was cut in the old Indian manner, to keep as much of the stone as the cutter dared.

treasure_idol_eye.name: Eye of a Temple Idol
treasure_idol_eye.lore: Some thief prised this green stone, great as a hen's egg, from the face of a temple idol with the gold eyelid still upon it, and in every tale of such a stone someone is hunted before the end.

treasure_viking_arm_ring.name: Viking Silver Arm-Ring
treasure_viking_arm_ring.lore: Chieftains of the North gave such rings to their warriors, and traders cut pieces from them to make payment, since silver went by its weight and never by its fairness. One end of this ring has already been spent in that manner, and what is left is heavy to carry for what it is worth.

treasure_saxon_brooch.name: Saxon Garnet Brooch
treasure_saxon_brooch.lore: A Saxon goldsmith made this brooch of gold and set it with hundreds of garnets, each as thin as a fingernail, over gold foil that throws back the light. With work like this upon them the kings of his people went into the ground.

treasure_solidus_purse.name: Byzantine Solidus Purse
treasure_solidus_purse.lore: Constantine the emperor first struck the gold solidus, and for seven hundred years those who followed him never lessened its weight of gold, so that merchants trusted it from Ireland to China. A pouch of such honest old coin is worth more than its weight in gold.

treasure_celtic_torc.name: Celtic Gold Torc
treasure_celtic_torc.lore: Chiefs and queens of the Celts wore the torc of twisted gold, and a Roman historian has written that Boudica rode to battle with such a great necklace upon her. With a pound of gold about the throat, none could doubt who was the ruler.

treasure_gulf_pearls.name: String of Gulf Pearls
treasure_gulf_pearls.lore: The divers of Bahrain went down from dawn until dusk into the warm sea, upon one breath and with a stone bound to the foot, and often they rose empty-handed. Each natural pearl on this string is a dive that was rewarded.

treasure_silver_candelabra.name: Silver Candelabra
treasure_silver_candelabra.lore: Some great house once lit its hall with these five branches of solid silver. They are fair but worth less than their weight in gold coin, and though a trader will give something for them they will be a heavy load for your back.

treasure_jade_bi.name: Liangzhu Jade Disc
treasure_jade_bi.lore: Five thousand years ago the people of Liangzhu in China laid upon their dead the bi, a flat disc of jade with a hole in its midst. No knife will cut that stone, and they laboured with sand and water for months to grind a single one.

treasure_arras_tapestry.name: Arras Tapestry
treasure_arras_tapestry.lore: The weavers of Arras were so renowned that the English called every wall hanging by the name of that town, and it was behind an arras in Hamlet that Polonius hid and met his death. These twenty pounds of wool and silk came from their looms, and are as wretched to carry as they are beyond price.

treasure_gold_idol.name: Gold Idol
treasure_gold_idol.lore: This squat god has no worshippers left, and he who cast him in solid gold took no care to make him fair, but gave him ten pounds in weight, which is much to carry when one must run.

treasure_gold_rhyton.name: Persian Gold Rhyton
treasure_gold_rhyton.lore: The kings of ancient Persia drank from horns of solid gold, each ending in the shape of a beast. Upon this one a winged lion roars, and its price would equal a city's taxes for a year.
